literature_name: Roseburia (the GTDB genus also holds genomes NCBI names Agathobacter, i.e. Eubacterium rectale)
name_note: The input row shows most genomes in this GTDB genus carry the NCBI names Agathobacter or Roseburia, so GTDB g__Roseburia is broader than the classical genus Roseburia and takes in Agathobacter rectalis (formerly Eubacterium rectale).

sentences.text: Roseburia are obligately anaerobic, Gram-positive, slightly curved rods that move with several subterminal flagella; named species include R. intestinalis, R. hominis, R. inulinivorans, R. faecis and R. cecicola.
They are gut commensals that ferment dietary components and produce short-chain fatty acids, mainly butyrate, which affects colonic motility and immune maintenance.
In faeces from healthy volunteers, probes for Roseburia and Eubacterium rectale relatives each detected about seven per cent of all bacteria counted.
Roseburia and Eubacterium members can grow on human milk oligosaccharides and cross-feed on mucin glycans, pathways linked to their colonisation of the early-life gut.
Studies have associated shifts in Roseburia abundance with several diseases; Eubacterium rectale was transferred to the related new genus Agathobacter as Agathobacter rectalis.
